review_output: {"summary":"I reviewed only the supplied files and found no BLOCKER or MAJOR defects. The 200-character title bound, the longer funnel step path, the slug cap of 100, the generic failure copy and the fail-closed schedule checks match the stated repairs. The remaining items are MINOR or NIT: the calendar relies on an unseen parser for its year ceiling, rescheduled events carry no SEQUENCE, and the component click path has no test. I did not run or certify any build, test or browser behavior.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/webinar-calendar.ts","area":"createWebinarCalendar, date guards (the line checking start/end/now years)","issue":"The upper year bound for start and end depends entirely on the imported parseFunnelWebinarSettings. The local guards check only `< 1` for start and end, and check both bounds for `now`. If the parser is later loosened, `utc(start)` or `utc(end)` would emit an extended-year string such as `+010000…`, which is invalid iCalendar.","evidence":"The local guard is `start.getUTCFullYear() < 1 || end.getUTCFullYear() < 1 || now.getUTCFullYear() > 9999`. It has no `start/end > 9999` check. The calendar test covers `+010000` only through the parser path, and the parser source is not in the supplied scope.","impact":"There is no current exploit, because the parser is said to reject these dates. This is a regression risk: the calendar's own output validity rests on a distant module's contract.","recommended_fix":"Add a cheap local assertion that start and end years are between 1 and 9999, or check that `utc(start)` and `utc(end)` match `/^\\d{8}T\\d{6}Z$/`.","required_test":"Keep the `+010000` calendar test.
